title: ATR-barrier study: ARO's architecture trained on 037's ATR-scaled triple barrier (tradeable rows), without (A) and with (B) the 037 composite's 7 member columns as inputs -- S1 screen, then S2 as a width-book sizer
label: PROVISIONAL -- one era (2023-26). The tbatr label, the composite members and every comparator's results were read on all halves before this file; no tbatr-trained model, score or backtest exists. Nothing is adopted or promoted.
why: 034's fixed-% triple-barrier model learned volatility (all-bar AUC 0.617 on its own label) but not direction where we trade (candidate AUC 0.525; 0.51 on tbatr) -- research/tb_model/check.json. The ATR-scaled label removes the volatility shortcut; 037 found direction signal on it (composite candidate AUC 0.554 / 0.552 vs ARO 0.541 / 0.539). Arm B asks whether those indicators help a model learn it.
label_definition: framework labels_triple_barrier / _sell with pt = sl = 1e-9, atr_scale 4.0 (ATR(14) Wilder), horizon 48, min_gain / min_loss None, post-label peak filter OFF (LABEL_PEAK_FILTER False, model-key attribute): BUY = up 4xATR first, SELL = down first, HOLD = timeout / tie. Checked before this file: equal to 037's label:tbatr_buy on SOL, 199,152 rows, 0 mismatches
training: per fold f00-f14, research.candidate_training.train --model TBA / TBB (seed 1, cs_aro's params snapshot), TRAIN_ROW_FILTER volume > 0 (last bar of each window); everything else ARO's (architecture, horizon, scaler for ARO's 24 columns)

cs_tbb.inputs: ARO's 24 + 7 composite members (user_data/data/tb_inputs, table_sha d84f8123ea593215: 037-cache columns, trailing z 2880 / min 960, clip +-5, /5)

s1.rows: test windows f00-f14, tradeable bars (data_ok AND volume > 0), label:tbatr_buy defined (timeouts / ties excluded)
s1.pass: per arm: median gbb-candidate AUC of p_buy above ARO's in BOTH halves (research/tb_model/screen.py)
s1.reported: all-bar AUC; candidate-bar MCC of BUY-argmax (the MCC without the gbb-setup shortcut); the 037 composite's candidate AUC per fold; B vs A (inputs_help_both_halves = B's candidate AUC above A's in both halves)

s2.design: cs_aro's: the model's p_buy as the capital-neutral width-book sizer, research/control_sizer/pick.py --plan plan_cs_<arm>.json (validation-tail run starts, 0.5 share, 4 dp, verified), 15-fold backtest
s2.instrument: research/xmodel_sizer/instrument.arm_check (cs_aro's checks; tag check against the arm's own test-window table signals/CS_TB?_fNN; entries without a score <= 1%)
s2.pass: cs_aro's bar: judge_one PASS vs w_aro AND wf_aro_g24 (small-margin rule)
s2.question: judge_one(arm, cs_aro): PASS = both half gains > 0, not WORSENED -- the tbatr-trained sizer beats the current ARO sizer

small_margin_rule: if any primary half gain is < 1 pp, a PASS is INCONCLUSIVE
seen_before: 037 tbatr screens (all halves, all and tradeable bars), composite and its members
cs_aro, w_aro, wf_aro_g24, cs_arov, cs_cmp, cs_mix results
question: can ARO's model learn direction (tbatr) on tradeable bars better than ARO, do the 037 indicators help it, and does that make a better width-book sizer than cs_aro?
